traits.label: Ecology
traits.text: Saprobic, primarily found on dead or dying wood of hazel species (sometimes found on other hardwood species), contributes to wood decay and is commonly found on fallen branches and dead trunks in forests and woodland areas
traits.raw: 🍂 Saprobic, primarily found on dead or dying wood of hazel species (sometimes found on other hardwood species), contributes to wood decay and is commonly found on fallen branches and dead trunks in forests and woodland areas

traits.label: Microscopy
traits.text: Spores ellipsoid to fusiform, 8–12 x 3.5–5 µm, smooth, and feature a distinct germ slit that runs the length of the spore, perithecia are embedded within a dark brown to black stromatic tissue, which forms irregular crusts on the surface of the host wood

traits.label: Overview
traits.text: Common ascomycete fungus primarily found on the dead or dying wood of hazel tree. The fungus produces dark brown to black, cushion-like stromata that form irregular crusts on the surface of the wood. These stromata house the perithecia, from which the dark, smooth spores are released
